decision: Integrate the stack in the order #526, #528, #524, #525, #527, #529, #530 and push each PR's resolutions by merging forward (feat/multi-tenant merges feat/substrate-ui and is retargeted onto it); no branch is rebased or force-pushed
rationale: #528 already carries #526's commit byte for byte, and #524/#525/#527/#529 merge cleanly in that order; only #530 conflicts with the substrate branches, and its resolutions touch #529 routes, so #530 must sit on #529. Merge-forward keeps every pushed commit and needs no force-push, which the repo guardrails reserve for explicit operator approval
alternatives: Rebasing #530 onto #529 (rewrites 8 reviewed commits and needs a force-push); keeping #530 on main (its resolutions cannot apply without #527/#529, and the substrate PRs would then need the resolutions instead, mixing concerns)

decision: Substrate session ownership delegates to lib/tenancy/ownership.ts: canAccess/filterVisible call requireOwnerOrAdmin/filterOwned, Caller is built from a Principal with callerFromPrincipal (owner key = ownerKeyFor), and listVisible compares lower(owner_subject) = lower($1)
rationale: #530 merge note 1: one gate decides every owner-scoped surface; the shared gate lowercases owner keys while the old canAccess compared case-sensitively, so the SQL filter is made case-insensitive to agree with it
alternatives: Keeping substrate's own Caller/canAccess (two gates can drift); replacing Caller with Principal throughout lib/substrate (larger diff in reviewed #527 code for no behavioural gain)

decision: /api/substrate/* use requirePrincipal: create and attach need terminal:exec; End, DELETE, Suspend, Resume and the #529 egress PUT need containers:write; list, get, config and egress/validate only authenticate; admin routes authenticate then keep #529's adminOnly 404
rationale: #530 merge note 2. The egress PUT mutates a session's sandbox policy, the same class as suspend/resume; validate changes nothing. Admin routes keep 404 for non-admins (a permission check would answer 403 and disclose the surface)
alternatives: requirePrincipal('admin:...') on admin routes (403 discloses); terminal:exec on egress PUT (it does not open a terminal)

decision: mode=substrate is dispatched after a terminal:exec check of its own and before the host-shell gate and the non-admin local-shell refusal; non-substrate modes keep #530's order (host-shell gate, then terminal:exec)
rationale: #530 merge note 4 requires terminal:exec before the substrate dispatch and the dispatch before the local-shell refusal; moving the shared terminal:exec check ahead of the host-shell gate would have changed #530's host-mode refusal reasons (11 host-shell-admin cases)
alternatives: One terminal:exec check before everything (changes host-mode refusal text the terminal UI shows)

decision: Substrate attach tickets carry perms, admin (admins only) and the session owner in the substrate claim; the hub stamps that owner on its recordings, records only with recording:write, and the message context carries the principal and recording owner
rationale: #530 merge note 3 (perms/admin; a ticket without perms is refused). Without the owner a hub recording had no owner and was admin-only, so a user could not see recordings of their own session; an admin viewing it must not take ownership (Codex round 2)
alternatives: Stamping the viewer's owner key (admin-started recordings hidden from the owner); no owner (admin-only recordings)

decision: A ticket that carries a substrate claim is refused for every non-substrate terminal mode
rationale: Codex full-diff review of #530 as integrated (HIGH): the attach ticket carries perms but no settings policy, so presented with mode=container it opened a container without the user's locks or mountRoot
alternatives: Adding settings/locked to substrate tickets (still lets one grant open arbitrary terminals; a single-purpose ticket is the narrower grant)

decision: Non-admins may not mount Docker named volumes in testcontainers or compose; anonymous volumes and confined binds are unchanged
rationale: Codex review (HIGH): named volumes skipped every tenant check, so a user could mount daax's own volumes (Postgres data, recordings and worktree-owner state) or another tenant's. Named volumes have no owner to check, so fail closed
alternatives: Tenant-prefixed volume names generated server-side (new naming contract; follow-up if non-admins need persistent volumes); an infrastructure-name denylist (incomplete by construction)

decision: Not fixed here, reported as blocking before non-admin exposure: the Traefik route to the --auth none code-server (reaches the whole workspace including .daax) and the symlink TOCTOU between canonical bind-source validation and Docker's own path resolution
rationale: Both are HIGH per Codex rounds 2 and 3, and neither is enforceable by a local change: the first needs a proxy admin gate that does not exist yet (idp-per-host-002); the second exists on main for #186 confinement and needs a mount broker (architectural, operator decision)
alternatives: Removing the code route (deployment decision); passing realpath to docker (ancestor directories stay swappable, and container-mode host-path translation changes)
